feature1.prompt: Feature 1: Refactoring to introduce a private scoring method. The objective is to add a new method, _score_samples, which replicates the functionality of score_samples but without performing input validation that may remove valid feature names. This change ensures that the core scoring logic is encapsulated in a private function and that score_samples simply delegates the work to _score_samples. The expected behavior is that the output of score_samples remains identical to that of the new _score_samples method, and no additional warnings or errors are introduced due to redundant validation.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature focuses on code refactoring. You need to add a new method _score_samples in the file sklearn/ensemble/_iforest.py which computes the anomaly scores without performing input validation. Modify the score_samples method so that it directly returns the value from _score_samples. Emphasize preserving the behavior of score_samples while eliminating redundant input validation to keep the original functionality intact.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sklearn/ensemble/_iforest.py; functions: score_samples (modify it to call _score_samples) and add a new private method _score_samples that computes the score without input validation (see code block modifications starting around line 428).

This change addresses the issue where fitting an IsolationForest with a DataFrame generates an unexpected warning about valid feature names. After the fix, fitting the model should behave as expected, with no warnings related to feature names even when using a non-'auto' contamination value.

feature2.entrypoint: File: sklearn/ensemble/_iforest.py; function: fit (specifically around the code block where offset_ is calculated, near the changes beginning at line 344). Replace the existing call to score_samples with a call to _score_samples for computing the offset_.
